vulnerabilities.name: SSTI via Python String Template Rendering (Jinja2/Mako/Tornado/Django)
vulnerabilities.description: Attacker-influenced input is concatenated or formatted into a template string that is then compiled and rendered by a Python template engine, instead of being passed as a context variable. The engine evaluates attacker-supplied expressions on the server.
vulnerabilities.notes: Flag when a source feeds the template string argument (via concatenation, f-string, % or .format()) rather than the render context. render_template_string('Hello {{ name }}', name=user_input) is safe; render_template_string('Hello ' + user_input) is not.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI via PHP Template Engines (Twig/Smarty/Blade)
vulnerabilities.description: User-controlled data is used to build a template string that is loaded through createTemplate(), a string: resource, or an in-memory loader, so the PHP template engine parses attacker-supplied expressions.
vulnerabilities.notes: Confirmed when the string passed to the template loader contains a source variable. Passing user data only as a render() context variable is not a finding.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI via Java Template Engines (FreeMarker/Velocity/Thymeleaf/SpEL)
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted input is used as template source, as a Thymeleaf preprocessed expression, or as a Spring Expression Language string, so the Java engine evaluates attacker-controlled expressions.
vulnerabilities.notes: For Spring MVC, returning a view name built from user input (e.g. return "user/" + param) lets Thymeleaf evaluate preprocessed expressions. Flag when the source reaches the template source, view name, or expression string.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI via Node.js Template Engines (EJS/Pug/Handlebars/Nunjucks/Lodash)
vulnerabilities.description: Request data is passed as the template source to compile/render functions of a Node.js template engine, or spread into engine options, allowing server-side expression and code evaluation.
vulnerabilities.notes: res.render(view, req.query) can also be dangerous: some engines read options such as outputFunctionName or settings from the data object. Flag both direct template-source flows and unfiltered option spreading.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI via Ruby ERB/Slim/Liquid String Templates
vulnerabilities.description: User-supplied data is interpolated into a string given to ERB.new, Slim, Haml, or inline render, so Ruby code embedded in the input is evaluated on the server.
vulnerabilities.notes: Liquid is sandboxed by design, so treat it as lower risk unless custom filters or tags expose unsafe functionality.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI via Go text/template Parse With Untrusted Input
vulnerabilities.description: A Go program builds a template from user-controlled text via template.New(...).Parse(...). The attacker can then read fields and call methods of any object in the template's data context, disclosing secrets or invoking dangerous methods.
vulnerabilities.notes: Severity depends on which objects are passed as template data. html/template escapes output but does not prevent template-source injection.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI Behavioral Fingerprint: Arithmetic Probe Evaluated in Response
vulnerabilities.description: A harmless arithmetic probe sent in a parameter (such as {{7*7}}, ${7*7}, <%= 7*7 %>, #{7*7}, {{7*'7'}}) is returned as its computed result instead of the literal text, proving the server evaluated template syntax. Differing outputs help fingerprint the engine family.

reflection_indicators.(?<![\\d{$#<%])49(?![\\d}]): response contains the computed value 49 where the literal probe string {{7*7}}, ${7*7}, <%= 7*7 %> or #{7*7} was sent and the literal is absent
reflection_indicators.7777777: response contains 7777777 for the probe {{7*'7'}}, which indicates Jinja2 or a similar Python engine; Twig returns 49 for the same probe
reflection_indicators.(?<![\\d{$#<%])343(?![\\d}]): response contains 343 for a {{7*7*7}} control probe, confirming expression evaluation rather than coincidence

vulnerabilities.notes: Always use a unique canary (e.g. send {{1337*3}} and look for 4011) and a control request with the literal text to avoid false positives from numbers that already appear on the page. Confirm that the literal probe is NOT echoed back unchanged.

vulnerabilities.name: SSTI Indicator: Template Engine Syntax Error Leaked in Response
vulnerabilities.description: Sending malformed template syntax (such as an unbalanced {{, ${, <% or #{) causes the server to return a template-engine parse or render error. This confirms user input reaches a template parser and reveals which engine is in use.

reflection_indicators.jinja2\\.exceptions\\.(TemplateSyntaxErr: Jinja2 template error exposed in the response

vulnerabilities.notes: A leaked error alone does not prove exploitability, but it confirms that user input reaches a template parser. Treat it as a strong lead and follow up with the arithmetic-probe check.

vulnerabilities.name: Client-Side Template Injection (AngularJS Expression Evaluation)
vulnerabilities.description: A page running AngularJS 1.x (inside an ng-app scope) reflects user input into the DOM. Angular evaluates {{ }} expressions found in the reflected text, so the input can execute in the browser even when HTML special characters are encoded.
vulnerabilities.notes: Confirm by reflecting {{7*7}} inside the ng-app scope and checking whether 49 is rendered in the DOM. Only AngularJS 1.x is affected; modern Angular (2+) does not evaluate template expressions from the DOM.

vulnerabilities.name: Template Debug Mode / Verbose Error Pages Enabled
vulnerabilities.description: The application runs with debug or verbose-error settings that expose stack traces, template source snippets, and an interactive console. This helps attackers discover and fingerprint SSTI and can by itself allow code execution.

reflection_indicators.Whoops! There was an error|Symfony Excep: Symfony/Laravel debug error page with template context
reflection_indicators.Whitelabel Error Page: Spring Boot default error page (check whether stack traces are exposed)

vulnerabilities.notes: This is a mitigation-gap finding. Pair it with an SSTI sink or probe finding to assess real exploitability. Debug mode should never be reachable in production.

vulnerabilities.name: Template Engine Sandbox Disabled or Unsafe Configuration
vulnerabilities.description: The template engine is configured without a sandbox or with unsafe options (autoescape off, unrestricted object exposure, dangerous globals), so any template injection that occurs can escalate directly to code execution.
vulnerabilities.notes: Prefer jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment, FreeMarker's SAFER_RESOLVER, Twig's SandboxExtension, and Smarty's security policy. Sandboxes reduce impact but do not replace keeping user input out of template source.
